amygdalus communis.d: small bushy deciduous tree native to Asia and North Africa having pretty pink blossoms and highly prized edible nuts enclosed in a hard green hull; cultivated in southern Australia and California

amygdalus communis amara.d: almond trees having white blossoms and poisonous nuts yielding an oil used for flavoring and for medicinal purposes

amyl.d: a hydrocarbon radical that occurs in many organic compounds

amyl alcohol.d: a mixture of 2 or more isomeric alcohols; used as a solvent and in organic synthesis

amyl nitrate.d: a vasodilator that is sometimes used to treat angina pectoris

amylase.d: any of a group of proteins found in saliva and pancreatic juice and parts of plants; help convert starch to sugar

amyloid.d: (pathology) a waxy translucent complex protein resembling starch that results from degeneration of tissue
a non-nitrogenous food substance consisting chiefly of starch; any substance resembling starch

amyloid plaque.d: a plaque consisting of tangles of amyloid protein in nervous tissue (a pathological mark of Alzheimer's disease)

amyloid protein plaque.d: a plaque consisting of tangles of amyloid protein in nervous tissue (a pathological mark of Alzheimer's disease)

amyloidosis.d: a disorder characterized by deposit of amyloid in organs or tissues; often secondary to chronic rheumatoid arthritis or tuberculosis or multiple myeloma

amylolytic.d: of or related to the process of amylolysis

amylum.d: a complex carbohydrate found chiefly in seeds, fruits, tubers, roots and stem pith of plants, notably in corn, potatoes, wheat, and rice; an important foodstuff and used otherwise especially in adhesives and as fillers and stiffeners for paper and textiles

amyotonia.d: lack of normal muscular tension or tonus

amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.d: thickening of tissue in the motor tracts of the lateral columns and anterior horns of the spinal cord; results in progressive muscle atrophy that starts in the limbs

amytal.d: the sodium salt of amobarbital that is used as a barbiturate; used as a sedative and a hypnotic

amyxia.d: a condition in which no mucus in produced
